## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

# 🤯 OMG — Oh My GitHub ### 🚀 One Prompt In. A Full Game or App Out. 🚀 [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-🔥%20works-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/denaidark/OhMyGithub?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/issues) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Actions-automated-2088FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-OpenCode-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://opencode.ai/) ```text ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ DESCRIBE IT → BUILD IT → TEST IT → PLAY IT ║ ║ ║ ║ One GitHub issue. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? | 🎯 Use case | ✨ Example | |---|---| | 🎮 Arcade games | Breakout, Space Invaders, Asteroids, Match-3 | | 🧩 Puzzle games | Word games, logic puzzles, card games | | 🏃 Interactive demos | Physics experiments, simulations, visual toys | | 📊 Dashboards | Filters, charts, status panels, analytics views | | 🛠️ Internal tools | Trackers, generators, small workflow apps | | 🌐 Landing pages | Product pages, portfolios, interactive showcases | | 🧪 Prototypes | Turn a product idea into a runnable proof of concept | | 📱 Browser apps | Responsive tools that work on desktop and mobile | ## 🧰 What Happens Automatically? > **The workflow is the product.** - 📥 Checks out your repository and the shared OpenCode skills. - 🏷️ Synchronizes `model/*` and `skill/*` labels. - 🧭 Reads issue labels to select the model and requested skills. - 🤖 Runs OpenCode against the current project. - 🧪 Runs a second verification prompt after implementation. - 🌐 Starts the app and checks the local runtime. - 🔗 Creates a temporary public preview URL when verification passes. - 🔀 Creates and pushes an `opencode/` branch. - 🕹️ Adds an `Open Project` link backed by the repository path, with full-commit links retained for compatibility. - 💬 Posts progress and access details back to the issue. - 🧹 Cleans up temporary tunnels and runner processes. ## 🏷️ Model and Skill Labels Labels let you control the workflow without editing YAML. ```text model/opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free skill/load-sketchfab-threejs skill/gauntlet-loop ``` The workflow validates the selected labels, passes them into OpenCode, and records the resolved model and skills in the run logs. Shared skills are discovered from: ```text .agents/skills//SKILL.md ``` ## 🔄 OpenCode Workflow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Trigger] --> B[Prepare project] B --> C[Run build.md] C --> D[Run verify.md] D --> E{Public app works?} E -- No --> F[Run public-app-fix.md] F --> E E -- Yes --> G[Run completion-report.md] G --> H{Screenshots exist?} H -- No --> I[Run screenshot-evidence.md] I --> H H -- Yes --> J[Commit and push] J --> K[Create immutable project link] K --> L[Publish report] L --> M[Complete] ``` ## 🏗️ Architecture ```text ┌──────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ GitHub issue │ ──▶ │ GitHub Actions │ ──▶ │ OpenCode │ │ + issue text │ │ runner + labels │ │ + .agents │ └──────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └──────┬───────┘ │ ┌─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ Build code Run tests Verify app │ │ │ └─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┘ ▼ ┌────────────────────────┐ │ Commit store + preview │ └────────────────────────┘ ``` ## 🔐 Security and Access - 🔑 You do not need to create or store a project-specific AI API key. - 🖥️ You do not need to operate a dedicated build server. - ☁️ Execution happens in GitHub Actions. - 🔒 Temporary SSH and preview access exists only for the workflow run. - 👀 Review the generated commit before integrating it. - 🛡️ Restrict who can apply the `OpenCode` label in repositories that accept public issues. > “No servers needed” means no servers for you to provision or maintain. The workflow still uses GitHub-hosted Actions infrastructure and temporary workflow services. ## 📁 Project Structure ```text 📦 OMG ├─ .github/workflows/opencode.yml # 🤖 Main issue-to-project workflow ├─ wiki/opencode.md # 📖 Workflow and session notes ├─ wiki/testing.md # 🧪 Verification guidance └─ AGENTS.md # 🧭 Repository instructions ``` ## 🧪 Local Validation Validate the workflow definition before pushing changes: ```sh actionlint .github/workflows/opencode.yml git diff --check ``` ## 🐛 Troubleshooting | Problem | What to check | |---|---| | The workflow did not start | Confirm the `OpenCode` label is applied to the issue. | | A skill was not selected | Add a matching `skill/` label. | | The app URL is missing | Check the local app verification step and runner log. | | The PR was not created | Confirm OpenCode produced a diff and the workflow reached the PR step. | | The workflow ran unexpectedly | Tighten the trigger condition and trusted-user policy. | ## 🤝 Contributing Ideas, skills, game templates, verification improvements, and workflow fixes are welcome. 1. Open an issue describing the improvement. 2. Add the `OpenCode` label when you want the workflow to prototype it. 3. Review the generated commit and Open Project page carefully. 4. Add tests and runtime proof for workflow changes. ## ⭐ The Pitch The old workflow was: idea → tickets → scaffolding → setup → implementation → debugging → deployment.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a playable 2D D&D dark-fantasy colony sim with an open world and deep RimWorld-inspired systems, delivered as a polished browser game.

## Requirements
- Must be 2D, D&D fantasy themed, open world, and very complex in the spirit of RimWorld.
- Needs working colony simulation, colonists, needs, skills, work priorities, building, resources, combat, events, research, quests, world expeditions, day/night, weather, and responsive desktop/mobile UI.
- Must run and be visually verified in-browser.

## Decisions
- Built with vanilla JavaScript + Vite and Canvas 2D, using DOM/CSS for the game interface.
- Chose a custom dark-parchment/brass visual style with serif typography and procedural map art.
- Implemented an original colony named Ashenreach with five starting D&D-style colonists and a ruined waystone quest.
- Added a full-screen title/start screen, scrollable codex panels, right-side inspector, minimap, world-map overlay, modals, and mobile bottom-sheet inspector.
- Tuned research, farming, and gathering rates downward after testing exposed overly fast progression.
- Used `window.__ashenreach` debug exposure for browser verification.

## Work State
### Completed
- Vite project scaffold, package/build pipeline, favicon, title screen, responsive styling.
- Procedural 64×44 open-world map with river, forest, crags, roads, ruins, resources, features, and mini-map.
- Five detailed colonists with races/classes, traits, skills, priorities, needs, health, mood, equipment, and thoughts.
- A* pathfinding, autonomous work assignment, gathering, construction, farming, cooking, crafting, research, doctoring, resting, eating, and wandering.
- Building system with 15 structures, blueprints, costs, research locks, placement preview, cancellation, deconstruction, and completed-building inspector.
- Day/night cycle, seasons, weather, lighting, fire glow, fireflies, rain/sleet, and eclipse effects.
- Combat with six enemy types, ranged projectiles, melee, bleeding, downed states, deaths/graves, loot, quest kill tracking, and raid spawns.
- Incidents, traveler recruitment, merchant trade, caches, omens, festivals, and expeditions with rewards.
- Research tree, quests, world-map overlay, chronicle log, notifications, event banners, help/menu/character modals.
- Desktop and mobile UI verified via Playwright; start screen, colony view, Work/Build/Arcana/World tabs, overview map, combat, and mobile inspector tested.
- Production build succeeds with `npm run build`.

### Active
- Final visual polish and verification pass.
- Need to re-check latest desktop screenshot and decide whether to add any remaining depth/polish.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Re-verify fresh production or Vite build in browser at 1440×900 and 390×844, checking console for runtime errors.
2. Exercise Build placement, priority cycling, expedition launch, research, and combat once more after the latest changes.
3. Consider additional visual polish only if verified issues remain; avoid destabilizing working systems.
4. Ensure final screenshots and `npm run build` are clean.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: game bootstrapping, actions, input/pan/zoom/pinch, render loop, mobile selection behavior.
- `src/sim.js`: simulation core, colonists, jobs, combat, events, research, quests, expeditions.
- `src/render.js`: Canvas world renderer, lighting/weather, minimap, overview world map.
- `src/ui.js`: all HTML panel rendering, inspectors, toasts, modals, tab interactions.
- `src/content.js`: D&D content definitions for races, classes, traits, buildings, research, enemies, incidents, expeditions.
- `src/world.js`: world generation, feature placement, A* pathfinding, walkability helpers.
- `src/style.css`: complete dark-fantasy UI styling and responsive/mobile layouts.
- `index.html`: app shell, HUD, panels, start screen, overlays.
- `package.json`: Vite scripts and dependency setup.
- `screenshots/final-desktop.png`: latest desktop colony screenshot.
- `screenshots/mobile-game2.png`: latest mobile game screenshot.
- `screenshots/overview2.png`: latest open-world map screenshot.
- `/tmp/opencode/vite.log`: Vite dev server log.
- `/tmp/opencode/vite.pid`: background Vite process PID.

## Important Context
- Dev server currently runs at `http://localhost:3002`; Playwright session name is `ash`.
- `playwright-cli click` requires a selector, not raw coordinates; use `mousemove <x> <y>` then `mousedown`/`mouseup` for map clicks.
- Last build passed; last browser console log contained only stale favicon 404s from before the favicon fix.
- The desktop UI starts with `Elara Voss` selected; mobile intentionally starts with the inspector closed until a colonist/building is tapped.
- Current initialization: `state.speed = 0` on load, then `Start Game` sets speed to 1.
- No sound assets; a subtle WebAudio drone is created after Start Game.
- Changes are uncommitted in the working tree.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
/usr/bin/time -p node "${RUNTIME_DIR:?}/scripts/default-capture.mjs"
## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

Built **Ashenreach**, a complete browser-based dark-fantasy colony sim in the repo.

**What’s included**
- Procedural 64×44 open world with river, forests, crags, roads, ruins, landmarks, and a minimap/overview map
- Five unique D&D colonists with races, classes, traits, skills, needs, moods, health, gear, and work priorities
- Autonomous jobs: gathering, mining, farming, cooking, crafting, research, construction, doctoring, resting, guarding
- 15 buildings with blueprints, research locks, placement previews, deconstruction, and toggles
- Combat with melee/ranged attacks, bleeding, downed colonists, deaths, graves, loot, and escalating raids
- Day/night, seasons, weather, lighting, fire glow, particles, and eclipse effects
- Research tree, quests, expeditions, traders, travelers, caches, omens, festivals, and a world map
- Responsive desktop and mobile UI, including mobile bottom-sheet inspector and touch pan/pinch controls
- Title screen, field manual, chronicle menu, event banners, notifications, and full chronicle log

- Tested production build in Chromium at 1440×900 and 390×844

The Sundered Marches · Year 732

ASHENREACH

A dark-fantasy colony chronicle of survival, sorcery, and stubborn hope.

❖

Five exiles. One broken waystone. An open world that remembers every choice.
Build a haven, bargain with strange powers, and keep the fire burning.

◈ Living colony⚔ Tactical raids✦ Deep arcana◉ Open world

A self-contained browser chronicle · Sound suggested

THE SUNDERED MARCHES
Click anywhere on the map to travel there · Drag the map to look around

We need implement:

1. Multiple starting scenarios.
2. Narrator like Randy Random — storyteller with random events intensity / cadence.
3. Choose where to spawn (world map tile selection).
4. Choose colonists before starting.

This requires a new game setup flow: title -> scenario selection -> spawn selection -> colonist selection -> start.

Need be mindful of existing createGame(seed) generating colony with fixed buildings/colonists and camp. We can refactor createGame to accept options: state setup. Approaches:

- Add a `createWorld(seed)` or expose `createGame` with options that generate world, add initial buildings at chosen location, add selected colonists, apply scenario.
- Setup UI in DOM: new full-screen setup overlay, with screens: scenario cards, spawn map, colonist roster. Or an integrated start flow after clicking Start Game. Title screen currently start. Could redesign start screen to "Begin a Chronicle" then setup. Scenario cards maybe on title? Better: start screen -> setup overlay with 3 steps (Scenario, Landing, Company), then start.

Need preserve title aesthetic.

Player chooses where to spawn on the map. We need present overview map with candidate sites; maybe procedurally generated candidate campsites (5-7) with pros/cons. Could simply click anywhere walkable to set settlement center. Must ensure valid placement of initial buildings. Existing initial buildings around camp 29,22. We can create a site generation at a center with predefined relative layout and check buildability, adapting. Or offer 6 viable sites with names and traits.

User explicitly "With a plant to chose where to spawn" likely typo "a plan/plant?" Means "a place to choose where to spawn". So map spawn selection.

We can generate sites from world: choose land center tiles near river/forest etc. Candidate sites with names and modifiers. Use an interactive setup map canvas showing full world and site markers. Click to choose one. Also allow "Survey another region"? Could show 6 site pins. Need ensure initial buildings fit. We'll generate candidate sites by scanning map for open areas around center (buildable 11x11), water adjacency etc. Existing world gen campX/campY fixed at 29,22? Let's inspect world.js.

actions.priority(btn.dataset.cid, btn.dataset.work, v >= 4 ? 1 : v + 1); } else if (action === 'research') actions.research(id); else if (action === 'expedition') actions.expedition(id); else if (action === 'stop-build') actions.stopBuild(); else if (action === 'open-overview') actions.openOverview(); else if (action === 'close-modal') closeModal(); else if (action === 'restart') actions.restart(); else if (action === 'speed') actions.speed(Number(btn.dataset.speed)); }); document.querySelectorAll('.tab').forEach(t => t.addEventListener('click', () => { state.uiTab = t.dataset.tab; state.dirty = true; lastLeft = ''; renderLeft(true); renderBottom(); })); document.querySelectorAll('.speed-btn').forEach(b => b.addEventListener('click', () => actions.speed(Number(b.dataset.speed)))); content.text:
Renderer overview hardcodes roads/camp. We need update to use world.camp. We could minimally change camp site positions and use state.world.campX/campY. Roads should originate from new camp; route existing roads? World generation roads hardcoded from old camp. Spawn elsewhere would still have old roads but okay if we change camp location, roads not connected. Better support dynamic adjustments. Let's architect robustly: ### Scenario system Create `SCENARIOS` in content.js: - `ashenreach` default ("A Fire in the Dark"): 5 colonists? choose 5 of roster? Starting resources normal, starting structures baseline. Crash-landed exiles, balanced. - `crash` "The Broken Caravan": 3 survivors, less food, more silver/crystal?, damaged supplies, harder; 3 colonists selected from available? User selects colonists; scenario may limit count. - `frontier` "The Last Outpost": 4 colonists, more starting materials, palisade partially built? Defense scenario, raids sooner. - `cult` "The Ash Covenant": 3 colonists, high research/crystal, low food, eerie; scenario start building shrine? Need not overcomplicate. - Maybe `tutorial` "A Quiet Hearth" easier narrator / 6 colonists, more supplies. Each scenario has: id, name, subtitle, desc, difficulty, colonistCount, resources, researchPoints, startBuildings variant, narrator intensity modifiers? quests, modifiers (raidMultiplier, foodMultiplier, morale?), startingResearch, banner text, color/icon. Keep implementation deterministic. Narrator like Randy Random: - Add `NARRATORS`: - `randy` "Randy Random" (chaotic: random intervals, can be extremely kind or cruel, event power swing) - `calm` "The Quiet Warden" (gentle, longer intervals, lower raid weights) - `grim` "The Hollow Choir" (harsh, shorter intervals, stronger raids) - maybe "The Chronicler" (balanced per scenario?). The request "plus a narrator like randy random" implies at least Randy Random. Offer 3 narrators with distinct behavior. Randy selects events with wide variance and random interval; "like Randy Random". - Narrator selection needed in setup. Could combine with scenario screen, each scenario may suggest narrator, but player can pick. Implement narrator state: ``` narrator: { id, name, ... } storyteller: { nextIncident: {day, hour}, intensity: 1, mood: '...' lastIncident, eventCount, pulse } ``` Existing `nextIncident` is simple. Extend `scheduleNextIncident(state)` that uses narrator: - interval base ranges e.g. randy: 5-18 hours; calm: 14-30; grim: 6-14. - severity multiplier; Randy rolls a "temper" each incident: 0.65-1.75 and event weight adjust. - Event pool weighted by narrator/circumstance. Existing triggerIncident chooses from all incidents with minDay. Need make narrator influence: - choose event class (threat/boon/neutral) weights from narrator. Randy: random class 45% threat, 30% boon, 25% neutral; calm 20/45/35; grim 55/18/27. Then choose from that class. - Randy can have "wild swing" chance causing double event count or bonus resources. - escalate based on wealth/colonist count (RimWorld style) and scenario difficulty. - Add narrator log lines in UI / setup and maybe a HUD narrator indicator. The narrator should be visible in game: right panel? A "Storyteller" card in colony tab or bottom? Add compact HUD indicator near chrono? Could place a narrator badge in colony tab with next omen? User asked narrator; it should be present and noticeable. Add in left colony a "The Storyteller" strip showing narrator name + last event/temper? Or a modal accessible via small button. Maybe add top HUD button "Narrator" with icon. Better: in colony left panel under stats, a small "Storyteller" card with name, style, "The tale is in Randy's hands." and next sign? Also menu can show. Add a dedicated clickable button in HUD with a mask icon near help? Could clutter. Add left panel card, enough. - Ensure events start after day 1/2; setup controlled. Randy Random schedules first incident after 6-14 hours with minDay. For quick demonstration maybe first at evening day 1. - Add ability to force incidents? Not requested. ### Spawn location selection Need setup map canvas. Options: - Add `
` with header brand, steps, footer. Steps: 1. Scenario + narrator 2. Landing site (interactive canvas of world) 3. Company (select colonists) Could show a single page with 3 columns? More manageable across viewport and mobile. Use step navigation. User must choose colonists before starting: - Show 12 candidates (mix fixed + randomly generated), select exactly N (scenario colonistCount, e.g. 5/3/4). Each candidate card includes race/class, traits, skills, priority aptitudes, and a re-roll button? They can choose from pool. - Need generate candidate pool deterministically per seed, ensuring enough skills. Use exported functions from sim or new file? Better add `generateRoster(seed, count=12)` in sim.js using makeColonist? makeColonist requires state.nextId and world no. Could create standalone `makeColonist` without state? It uses state.nextId for id. We can refactor id optional. Simpler: create candidates in main.js using a new exported helper from sim.js or content. But we need stats matching makeColonist. Could add `generateColonistPool(seed)` in sim.js that builds a temporary state-like object `{nextId: 1}` then makeColonist, and returns them, then on start, remap IDs. However the game state is created at load. We can generate world early and pool from seed. Flow challenge: currently `const state = createGame(732)` on load and renderer created. Setup needs world for map. We can still create state at load (with default camp), but then rebuild state on choice. State is const referenced widely by renderer/ui/actions. Recreating state means reassign let and update references? Renderer holds state reference, UI holds state. Easiest: add a `resetGame(options)` that mutates existing `state` object in place? Or create state after setup, but renderer/ui need state. We could modify main to create game once after setup but renderer/ui instantiate then. Yet start screen needs overlay map preview before started. We can draw a setup map separately without game renderer. Alternative: keep initial `state = createGame(seed, options)` but make options mutable `setup` and recreate full state via `Object.assign(state, newState)` then renderer.state? Renderer receives state object; if we mutate in place, renderer's reference stays and most fields update. UI also references state object. That works. Implement function `applyGame(state, opts)`? `createGame` can be updated to accept `options`, and `resetGame` compute newState then `Object.assign(state, newState)`; but arrays/objects replaced, and UI's captured `state` is same object so fine. Renderer closure uses state object; fine. Camera must recenter, resize remains. But renderer's cam initial center set from old world at creation; after reset, call renderer.centerOn(new camp...). Good. Need generate candidate pool across scenario changes; scenario defines count but pool should remain same or regenerate on scenario change. Could generate once per world seed at setup load. Need also select default first N. On scenario changes update required count and trim selection. Spawn sites generation: - World generation currently hardcodes camp clearing and initial resources at old coordinates; if choosing spawn elsewhere, those initial features remain at old camp and the new camp may have forest/features. We need modify world generation to accept site and adapt: - `generateWorld(seed, site)` where site = {x,y,name,id}. Clear camp area around site, generate roads from site? Existing roads anchored at 29,22. Could return campX/campY = site.x/y. - `generateFeatures(world, rng)` currently ring resources around camp hardcoded. Update ring relative to camp. - roads: generate from camp to destinations? Existing roads might not connect. Could add a road from new camp to nearest point? For visual, update road anchor start to campX,campY. Routes defined with camp start but other waypoints fixed. If spawn far, line to `[campX+1,30]` could cross. Better generate general roads from camp to fixed landmarks? Let's redesign slightly: - Main north-south road along `[campX, campY] -> [campX+4, 38] -> [campX+6, 43]` etc. But if camp is near bottom, weird. - Could leave roads at original map (they're "old roads") and new camp is off-road. This is plausible but some visuals. Add a short trail from camp to nearest old road via straight line using existing roads? Generate simple "camp trails": paths to [camp+?]. Maybe not essential. - Actually spawn site candidates can be chosen around existing roads and world landmarks. For simplicity, choose 6 candidate sites all in open areas, including original camp (29,22), others e.g. near north meadow, east woods, southern road, etc. Each starts with a local clearing (we can carve a 6-tile radius) and local ring resources. That gives real differences. Roads existing from old camp would be odd if not there, but could be interpreted as old trade roads crossing the Marches. Better update world roads to start at new camp, adding 3 roads. The overview roads updated from camp. - Need ensure all candidates are viable: open enough area for starting structures and resources. We can compute from base world before clearing? Simpler manual site list with coordinates and validate buildability by scanning; choose nearest viable fallback. Candidate sites: - "Waystone Rise" (29,22) original, balanced. - "River's Bend" (14,28?) near river; water access, fertile but exposed. Need clear. - "Whisperwood Edge" (20,14) forest; wood-rich, poor stone. - "Old Road Crossing" (36,36?) near road; trade, open. - "Cragwatch" (23,34?) near southwest crags; stone, harsh. - "Sunken Approach" (43,26?) near shrine; arcana, danger. We need validate random terrain. Let's generate world and scan. Could script with node importing world.js? ESM importing content. Use node `--input-type=module`. Let's evaluate coordinates of tiles, features, buildable footprint. But world gen currently clear only old camp. For candidate site viability we need 11x11 buildable after clearing? Starting buildings need about 11x11; we'll carve clearing radius 7 around site if not water/mountain? Water should not be cleared? Camp clearing currently only non-water. To avoid invalid, require center area has sufficient walkable tiles and no water within maybe 4. For each site we can clear grass/forest/dirt/ruin not water/mountain? Existing camp clearing does not alter water. Starting buildings maybe around center. Need robust auto layout. Alternative simpler: Every spawn site carves a 6.2 radius clearing (non-water) and starting compound layout as fixed relative to center; validate with `canPlace` but if overlap features cleared. Could build starting structures at relative coords from old layout: ``` campfire (0,0) tent (-3,-4) beds (-4,-1), (-4,0),(2,0),(3,0),(-4,1) stockpile(-6,2) workbench(3,2) researchDesk(4,-1) well(6,0) farm (-2,-5... etc) palisade... ``` For any site, clear area radius ~7 of features and make ground buildable (trees removed). But sites near water might have water in footprint; ensure site score chooses center with no water within radius 5. We can regenerate features after world clear so ring features removed within camp. Existing `generateFeatures` skips camp <6.3; candidates clear within 6.2. With buildings up to 6 tiles from center, could conflict. Use camp clear radius 7.2 and feature skip 7.5, plus ring resources at relative offsets ~7-9. Water in camp radius would remain; candidate sites chosen with no water within 7.5. That constrains: river at x~7-14. So River's Bend could be near x=17 y=28 with river view at distance 4. Good. Mountain crag inside radius? clearing doesn't change mountains. Candidate centers need no mountains within 7. Maybe clear mountain too? Visually could carve clearing from forest but not crag. Choose open. Could create sites adaptively: scan a grid for viable centers with buildable area, then select 6 spaced sites with different neighborhood scores. That's more robust and gives natural names based on nearby terrain: - For each center on grid (step 4) with 8-tile square clear of water/mountain, compute: - nearby wood count (forest tiles + tree features) - stone count (mountain/rock) - water proximity - ruin proximity - distance from other sites (>=10) - Pick 6 diverse: highest wood, highest stone, near water, near road, near ruins, most balanced. Known location names fixed per slot? Name based on feature: - "Waystone Rise" default - "Whisperwood Edge" if woods - "Stonecradle" if stone - "River's Bend" if water - "The Old Road" if road/dirt - "Shrine's Shadow" if ruin Can assign based on score. Need no dynamic guarantees? Better generate deterministic site list from world and pick. But setup map needs site previews, before state is finalized. Could call a function `buildSpawnSites(seed)` from world.js/sim.js that generates base world (seed) and computes candidates. Then `createGame` uses site to generate final world (with clearing) and features. Potential circular dependency: sim imports world; candidates computed in world.js. Good. Implement `findSpawnSites(seed)` in world.js: 1. `base = generateWorld(seed)` with camp old (clearing old area) — but when selecting a new site, need regenerate with chosen camp and clearing. 2. For candidate scanning, base tiles include old camp clearing and roads; acceptable. Could call `generateWorld(seed)` and use `world.tiles`. 3. Scan x 12..w-12, y 8..h-8 step maybe 3. For each, check 15x15 area (`|dx|<=7,|dy|<=7`) all walkable except forest (walk yes), no water/mountain; also ensure enough walkable. Score resources within radius 11. Avoid edges. Pick 6 via categories. But candidate site maybe overlapping landmark; filter if within 8 of special fixed points (shrine 47,29, grove 13,12, etc.) and old camp? The old camp can be included as default. We want variety. Also avoid spawn at mountains. We can pick: - First: closest viable to original camp 29,22 (Waystone Rise). - Then candidates maximizing wood, stone, water, road, ruin. With spacing >=12. Names. - Also difficulty hints: each site has "fertile/wood/stone/water/exposed/arcane". - Each has a `modifier` maybe no mechanical need, just flavor; but we can give small resource bonuses at start? e.g. extra starting wood if wooded, extra stone if crag, etc. That would make choice meaningful. Implement site.startBonus `{wood:+20}` etc. - Site card on map shows details and local resources. Need draw setup map with candidate sites. Could reuse drawOverview? It draws full state-dependent world, hardcoded locations. Better implement a separate `drawSetupMap(canvas, world, sites, selectedId, hoverId)` in render.js. Now world.js big edit. We'll replace generateWorld and generateFeatures, add findSpawnSites, worldLocations. Need careful.

Let's design exact code.

```
export function generateWorld(seed=732, spawn=null) {
 const campX = clamp(Math.round(spawn?.x ?? 29), 6, 57)
 const campY = ...
 ...
 // forest etc unchanged
 // roads dynamic after terrain features before camp clearing
 const rawRoads = [...]
 carve...
 // camp clearing radius 7.1 (non-water/mountain)
 // shrine clearing
 // ford
 // ruins
 const roads = rawRoads // maybe store simplified
 return {..., roads, spawnSite: spawn}
}
```
Roads coordinates can go out of bounds; carve loops should clamp.
- For static generation, base world clear at 29,22, shrine, crag, etc. If camp at new location, clear new; old camp remains grass? Original base world in `findSpawnSites` uses camp 29,22 generating clearing there. When final generateWorld with another spawn, the old camp clearing will NOT be there; fine (site finding not final map). Setup map still shows the old clearing at 29,22 even if not chosen. Slightly odd but acceptable: a clearing might appear in setup though final world differs. Could avoid by making `generateWorld(seed, spawn)` not clear at all for preview? Candidate sites selection base can use spawn 29,22. The preview map only visual; the chosen final map will differ only by chosen clearing. Difference subtle. Fine.
- But world roads in base preview anchored at 29,22; final anchored chosen. User may see road network change after start. Minor. Could generate preview with selected site each time selection changes; but map would shift and site viability already fixed. We could call drawSetupMap using `generateWorld(seed, selectedSite)` to preview exact. That's extra computationally cheap. Setup map can generate final preview world for selected site, while site scoring uses base world. But world object from findSpawnSites can be regenerated. Let's do in setup.js: `const previewWorld = generateWorld(seed, selectedSite)` for map; but then site pins from sites. That yields exact roads/clearing. Need import generateWorld. Fine. Or findSpawnSites returns previewWorld default. We'll handle in setup with generateWorld(seed, site) each render. It's fast. `world.locations` needed; can call makeWorldLocations.

- `makeWorldLocations(world, site)`:
```
const s = site || {x:world.campX,y:world.campY,name:'Waystone Rise'}
return [
 {id:'camp',name:'Ashenreach',x:world.campX,y:world.campY, icon:'✦', danger:0, blurb: site?.name || 'The colony fire', discovered:true},
 {grove...}
]
```
Use fixed landmark positions.
- In createGame set world.locations = makeWorldLocations(world, spawn).

`findSpawnSites(seed)` detailed:
```
